areas.name: Clarity
questions: Can you describe what your business does, and for whom, in one clear sentence?
Do you know what makes you a different choice from your closest competitors?
Does your team describe the business the same way you do?
areas.advice: Start with direction. A clear positioning and messaging foundation makes every later design decision easier.

areas.name: Identity
questions: Does your logo work at every size, from a profile picture to a signboard?
Do you have defined brand colours and fonts that you use every time?
Do you have brand guidelines someone new could follow without asking you?
areas.advice: Build the system. A logo suite, colour, typography, and guidelines turn a single mark into a recognisable brand.

areas.name: Website
questions: Does your website explain what you offer within the first few seconds?
Does your website look and work well on a phone?
Is there one obvious next step for a visitor—enquire, book, or buy?
areas.advice: Sharpen your website. A clear message, a responsive design, and one obvious next step turn visitors into enquiries.

areas.name: Consistency
questions: Do your social media, documents, and website look like they come from the same business?
Do your invoices, proposals, and business cards carry your brand?
Can you produce new marketing materials quickly, without reinventing the look each time?
areas.advice: Hold it together. Templates, stationery, and steady design support keep everything looking like one business.

bands.title: Well built.
bands.text: Your brand has strong foundations. The work now is keeping it consistent as the business grows.

bands.title: Taking shape.
bands.text: The essentials are in place, with a few gaps worth closing before they slow you down.

bands.title: Room to grow.
bands.text: Parts of your brand are working, but people are probably getting a mixed picture of the business.

bands.title: A fresh start.
bands.text: You are early—which is the easiest time to get the foundations right.
